findings.desc: CHK-011:adversarial:1 evidence mismatch: intent is "Remove the chain-smoke from validate.commands -> lattice validate no longer runs it; the regression must be caught by a committed test or the validate output audit" (i.e. detect de-registration of red-evidence-chain-smoke.js from lattice.config.json validate.commands). The bound evidence is packages/main/tests/red/red-w2c-wiring-detectability.mjs, which tests a DIFFERENT scenario entirely: stripping the compiled command-policy.js registration entry for red_evidence_quarantine/red_evidence_recover and asserting command-ownership-contract/lifecycle-registry-contract fail. It never touches lattice.config.json validate.commands nor red-evidence-chain-smoke.js at all. No committed test in the repo scans validate.commands for completeness against packages/main/src/tasks/*.ts, so removing the chain-smoke registration line from lattice.config.json today would go undetected by any committed mechanism. Note this same wiring-detectability test IS a strong match for CHK-011:adversarial:0's intent ("delete the command-catalog entry for red_evidence_quarantine"), suggesting the evidence binder cross-assigned it to the wrong intentRef and left adversarial:1 genuinely uncovered.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in b4fa4bbfad: new committed test red-w2c-validate-registration.mjs asserts red-evidence-chain-smoke.js is registered in lattice.config.json validate.commands (plus non-vacuity and dangling-source checks); CHK-011:adversarial:1 re-bound to it and CHK-011:adversarial:0 re-bound to red-w2c-wiring-detectability.mjs. RED verified by deleting the config entry.

findings.desc: CHK-001:edge:0 evidence is weaker than the sibling coverage in the same file. Intent: "Construct a green-confirm record; verify it has confirmsRecordId/confirmsRecordDigest/confirmsAssertionDigest but NO assertion/policySnapshot of its own". red-evidence-chain-smoke.ts section 1 (lines 180-197) proves this EXACT pattern for the quarantine record by hand-building a draft object and asserting field presence/absence with the `in` operator in a loop. For green-confirm (CHK-001:edge:0) the smoke never constructs a GreenConfirmRecordV2 instance at all -- it only calls greenConfirmOperationKey() (a function over primitive strings) and checks the GRN- id prefix (lines 333/338). The claim that this is adequate because "the field set is the compiled discriminated-union contract (green-confirm writer is W2e)" relies purely on TypeScript type erasure at compile time; nothing at runtime confirms a constructed green-confirm object omits assertion/policySnapshot the way the quarantine test does two sections above it. Building a synthetic GreenConfirmRecordV2 draft (as was already done for red-assert and quarantine, which also have no writer command registered by this story) and running the same `in`-based presence/omission loop would have been directly achievable without needing the W2e writer, and would match the sibling evidence quality used for every other operation in this same section.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in b4fa4bbfad: chain-smoke section 1 adds a synthetic GreenConfirmRecordV2 draft with an in-operator field-set loop asserting confirms fields and red baseline copies PRESENT and assertion/policySnapshot OMITTED. CHK-001:edge:0 re-bound.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/core/proofstory.ts:944 redEvidenceRecordSatisfied guards only isRedEvidenceV2(record) (exact schemaVersion==="proofstory.red_evidence.v2"); any record whose schemaVersion is set but NOT that exact string (a future v3, or a corrupted/malformed stored record) falls through to the v1 branch and crashes at record.observedFailure.trim() (:947-949) in the LIVE enforce gate — reproduced live: writing {schemaVersion:"proofstory.red_evidence.v3", operation:"red-assert", ...} (no observedFailure) into a real store and calling evaluateProofStoryDiagnostics throws TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading trim). This contradicts CHK-003s own title (skip EVERY non-v1 record) and the forward-compatibility fail-closed philosophy record-v2.ts:177 classifyRedRecordSchema documents (throws on unknown schemaVersion) — but classifyRedRecordSchema is never called from the gate path (only from its own smoke-test assertion in red-evidence-chain-smoke.ts:200-203), so the fail-closed guarantee it advertises is not actually wired to the one place (the live enforce gate) that the story exists to protect. RED signal A is fixed only for the specific known-v2 shape, not for the non-v1/non-v2 case its own doc comments claim to cover.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in b4fa4bbfad (one defect with F-004/F-005): schema discrimination is exhaustive and fail-closed via record-v2.ts:182 RedEvidenceSchemaError and :196 classifyRedRecordSchemaSafe, wired into store.ts:870 read path and proofstory.ts:949 gate predicate. Test red-w2c-schema-failclosed.mjs PASS; differential RED confirmed against the pre-fix tree.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/core/red-evidence/record-v2.ts:177-188 classifyRedRecordSchema (the CHK-002 adversarial fail-closed-on-unknown-schemaVersion guarantee) is declared and unit-tested in isolation but is NEVER CALLED from any real read path: store.ts:852 readRedEvidence does plain JSON.parse with zero validation, and proofstory.ts:944 redEvidenceRecordSatisfied only skips records whose schemaVersion is the LITERAL string proofstory.red_evidence.v2 (via isRedEvidenceV2) -- any OTHER/unknown schemaVersion (e.g. proofstory.red_evidence.v3, or a typo/corrupted value) falls through to the v1 branch and crashes at record.observedFailure.trim() (proofstory.ts:945) because such a record has no observedFailure field. Live-reproduced against the built dist: a red-evidence.json record {schemaVersion:proofstory.red_evidence.v3, id:RED-v3-1, operation:quarantine, ...} (no observedFailure) is silently accepted into records[] and then throws TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading trim) inside evaluateProofStoryDiagnostics -> redEvidenceSatisfied -> .some(redEvidenceRecordSatisfied), i.e. it crashes the LIVE dev/review/done enforce gate (devGateMode/reviewGateMode/doneGateMode all enforce). This directly contradicts CHK-002 adversarial:0 (a record with an unknown schemaVersion is rejected at parse/load time with a diagnostic, not silently accepted into the array) and reopens, for any non-v2 schema drift, the EXACT crash class (record.observedFailure.trim() on a fieldless control record) that CHK-003/RED-signal-A in this same story was built to close for v2 specifically. The only test exercising classifyRedRecordSchema (red-evidence-chain-smoke.ts:200-203) calls it directly as a standalone function, never through store.readRedEvidence or the actual gate pipeline, so the gap is untested end-to-end.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in b4fa4bbfad (one defect with F-003/F-005): classifyRedRecordSchema is now called from production - store.readRedEvidence classifies every record and fails closed on an unsupported schemaVersion; the gate predicate independently skips non-v1 records as defense in depth.

findings.desc: schemaVersion discriminant is NOT exhaustive — silent fall-through crashes the LIVE enforce gate: packages/main/src/core/red-evidence/record-v2.ts:152-158 isRedEvidenceV2() only recognizes the exact literal proofstory.red_evidence.v2 string; every production call site (proofstory.ts:944 redEvidenceRecordSatisfied, chain.ts:36 partitionChain, handlers/red-evidence.ts:53 findV2Record) uses isRedEvidenceV2 and treats anything that is NOT exactly v2 as v1 by default. The fail-closed helper classifyRedRecordSchema (record-v2.ts:177-188), whose own doc comment promises unknown schemaVersion values fail CLOSED per CHK-002s forward-compatibility rule, is dead in production — its ONLY caller anywhere in src/ is the smoke test (tasks/red-evidence-chain-smoke.ts), never proofstory.ts/chain.ts/red-evidence.ts. Repro: wrote a record with schemaVersion=proofstory.red_evidence.v3 (a hypothetical future/corrupted version) with no observedFailure field into a stores red-evidence.json and called evaluateProofStoryDiagnostics — it THROWS TypeError Cannot read properties of undefined (reading trim) at record.observedFailure.trim(), i.e. it reproduces the EXACT live-gate crash class CHK-003 was supposed to fix, for any schemaVersion other than the two known literals. This also silently violates CHK-002:adversarial:0 (unknown schemaVersion must be rejected at parse/load time with a diagnostic, not silently accepted) — nothing rejects it; it free-falls into the v1 code path and either crashes or (if the malformed record happens to carry v1-shaped fields) could silently satisfy/pollute the v1 gate verdict. Fix: isRedEvidenceV2 (or its call sites) must route through classifyRedRecordSchema (or equivalent) so an unrecognized schemaVersion throws/fails closed BEFORE reaching v1 field access, not fall through as if absent.
findings.resolvedReason: CORRECTED (round 4): the discriminant is exhaustive at all production call sites. The v1-only gate diagnostic invariance is proven by the committed test packages/main/tests/red/red-w2c-v1-verdict-invariance.mjs, which runs five v1-only scenarios through the real diagnostics and hashes the concatenated canonicalized full reports to sha256 2d584cc157e83ebb2f8396735f04d46946f0ba90d18a55d9fb2f263d706a11ec; the pre-fix tree produces the SAME digest, so no v1 verdict moved. NOTE: an earlier version of this resolution cited sha256 71c267a0a7372e9679d00b84be2e2b3480151bfa88939bddcae251aa750d95bc, which was reported by a subagent and is produced by NOTHING in the repository. That was an unbacked claim; it is retracted here and replaced by the reproducible digest above.

findings.desc: [codex host-B round-3] The three reverse-order companion cases that round 3 deliberately RETAINED (labelled vacuous) are still assertions in the evidence set that cannot fail: red-w2c-gate-guard.mjs:113 and :116, red-w2c-schema-failclosed.mjs:149 and :152, and red-evidence-chain-smoke.ts:287 and :290 (the artifact registered in lattice.config.json validate.commands). In each, a SATISFYING v1 record precedes the record under test, so Array.prototype.some() short-circuits and the record under test is never evaluated; all six assertions also pass against the pre-guard tree. Labelling them does not make them evidence. Fix per codex: order them [unsatisfying v1, record-under-test, satisfying v1] so the record under test IS evaluated while remaining non-leading — that turns a vacuous companion into a genuine mid-array placement scenario — or remove them. codex confirmed the four round-3 fixes themselves are sound and found no swallowed test conditions.

[orchestrator, same class as F-012] 35 of the 94 verificationEvidence notes cite BARE LINE NUMBERS of the COMPILED artifact (packages/main/dist/tasks/red-evidence-chain-smoke.js), and 0 cite a source location. Those citations are already stale on HEAD independently of any round-4 edit — verified: CHK-004:edge:0 cites line 254 but checkChainIntegrity([], null is at 244; CHK-001:edge:1 cites 297 (now 283) and a 'helper line 581' that exceeds the 580-line file; CHK-012:adversarial:1 cites 470 (now 451); CHK-009:adversarial:1 cites 541 (now 504). This is the F-012 defect class (a note pointing at something that is not there), and citing compiled-output lines is structurally wrong because every rebuild re-stales them. Fix: re-anchor each note to a STABLE reference — the SOURCE file plus its section name, helper/function name, or the assertion message — instead of a compiled line number. Each note must describe only what its own cited assertion does (copy-paste between notes is what produced F-012).
